# MethodCache: instructions for coding agents

Copy this file into your project as agent instructions, for example as `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, a Cursor
rule, a Claude Code skill or a section of `AGENTS.md`. It tells a coding agent how to add caching with MethodCache
correctly. Full docs: https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/README.md

## Adding caching to a service

1. The `MethodCache` package contains the library, the source generator and the analyzers. Nothing else is needed
   for in-memory caching.
2. Put `[Cache]` on the **interface** method, never on the class. Put `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = [...])]` on the
   interface methods that change the data. Don't change the implementation.
3. Register services as usual, then call `builder.Services.AddMethodCache()` **after** them.

```cs
public interface IProductService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:01:00", Tags = ["products"])]
    Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page);

    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product);
}

public sealed class ProductService(Database db) : IProductService
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<Database>();
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();   // any lifetime
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();                               // after your registrations
```

## Rules

- Only interface methods that return a value can be cached: sync, `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>`. Return a list, never
  a lazy `IEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`.
- Callers must use the interface. Calling the method from inside the class, or resolving the class itself, bypasses
  the cache.
- Keys are generated from the method and its arguments; don't write keys for `[Cache]` methods. A `CancellationToken`
  is not part of the key. Every value that changes the result must be a parameter.
- Tags take templates with a **parameter name** only: `"product:{id}"`. `"{product.Id}"` is not a template, stays
  literal and gives warning MCG015; add an `id` parameter instead. Use the same tags on the cached method and on its `[CacheInvalidate]`.
- Durations are `TimeSpan` strings: `Duration = "00:10:00"`. Other settings: `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead`,
  `FailSafe` (or `"off"`), `FailSafeTimeout`, `Version`, `Tags`, and a group name as the first argument.
- Cached objects are shared between callers: return immutable types such as records.
- For a type with only private state used as an argument, implement `ICacheKeyProvider`.
- For a client from a NuGet package with an interface, use
  `[assembly: CacheInterface(typeof(IClient), nameof(IClient.Method), Duration = "...")]` instead of a wrapper.
- Without an attribute, use `ICacheManager.GetOrCreateAsync(key, factory, o => o.WithDuration(...))` with an explicit,
  prefixed key such as `$"order:{id}"`.
- Fix every `MC` and `MCG` build diagnostic; each links to its explanation, and many have a code fix.
- In tests, register `NoOpCacheManager` (namespace `MethodCache.Extensibility`) after `AddMethodCache()` to turn
  caching off.

## Namespaces

- `MethodCache`: `[Cache]`, `[CacheInvalidate]`, `[CacheInterface]`, `ICacheManager`, `ICacheAdministrator`,
  `IRuntimeCacheConfigurator`, `MethodCacheKeys`, `MethodCacheMemoryOptions`, `Any<T>`, `ICacheKeyProvider`.
- `MethodCache.Extensibility`: `ISerializer`, `JsonCacheSerializer`, `ICacheKeyGenerator`, `JsonKeyGenerator`,
  `NoOpCacheManager`.
- `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection`: `AddMethodCache`, `AddMethodCacheFromConfiguration`,
  `AddMethodCacheRedis` (package `MethodCache.Redis`), `AddMethodCacheSqlServer` (package `MethodCache.SqlServer`).

<!-- source: docs/getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

MethodCache is not on nuget.org yet. Until it is, reference the projects from this repository (the
[demo's project file](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/samples/MethodCache.Demo/MethodCache.Demo.csproj) shows how). Once published:

```bash
dotnet add package MethodCache
```

The `MethodCache` package contains the library, the source generator and the analyzers. It supports .NET 8, 9 and 10.

## 1. Start from a service

A typical service talks to a database on every call:

```cs
public sealed class ProductService(Database db)
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

## 2. Put the attributes on its interface

`[Cache]` goes on interface methods that return data, `[CacheInvalidate]` on the methods that change it. The
implementation doesn't change:

```cs
public interface IProductService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:01:00", Tags = ["products"])]
    Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page);

    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product);
}

public sealed class ProductService(Database db) : IProductService
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

- `GetAsync(42)` is stored for ten minutes under a key built from the method and its argument
  (`...IProductService.GetAsync:42`). The `CancellationToken` is not part of the key.
- `"product:{id}"` is a tag template: `GetAsync(42)` is tagged `product:42`.
- `UpdateAsync(42, ...)` removes every entry tagged `products` or `product:42` once it has completed.

The attributes must be on the interface. On a class they do nothing, and the analyzer reports
[MC0001](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0001) with a code fix that moves them.

## 3. Register it

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<Database>();
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();   // any lifetime
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();                               // after your registrations
```

`AddMethodCache()` wraps every registered interface that has cached methods in its generated decorator and keeps the
lifetime you chose. Call it after your own registrations: a service registered later is not cached. If you don't
register an implementation at all, `AddMethodCache()` registers it as a singleton when it lives in the same project as
the interface.

Generic interfaces work the same way: `IRepository<User>` is cached for every closed type a class in your project
implements, such as `UserRepository : IRepository<User>`. An open generic registration such as
`AddScoped(typeof(IRepository<>), typeof(Repository<>))` is not cached; register the closed types instead.

## What can be cached

```cs
[Cache] Product Get(int id);                          // synchronous
[Cache] Task<Product> GetAsync(int id);               // Task<T>
[Cache] ValueTask<Product> GetFastAsync(int id);      // ValueTask<T>
[Cache] Task<Product?> FindAsync(string name);        // null results are cached too
```

- Synchronous methods, `Task<T>` and `ValueTask<T>` can be cached. A method that returns nothing has nothing to
  cache, so `[Cache]` on it is a build error ([MCG001](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg001),
  [MCG002](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg002)). So is a lazy `IEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`
  ([MCG014](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg014)): return a list.
- Exceptions are never cached: the next call runs the method again.
- Concurrent calls with the same arguments share one call to your method (stampede protection). A caller that cancels
  only stops its own wait.
- `null` results are cached. Turn that off with `CacheNullValues` on the [memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md), or
  per method with [conditional caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md).
- The cached object is returned as is, not copied. Treat cached results as read-only.

## Next steps

- Choose how long entries live: [Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md).
- Remove entries when data changes: [Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md).
- Change durations without a redeploy: [Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md).
- Share the cache between instances: [Distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/keys.md -->

# Cache keys

You never write keys for `[Cache]` methods. The generated decorator builds each key from the interface, the method
and the arguments, so two calls share an entry exactly when they call the same method with equal arguments.

```cs
public sealed record UserQuery(string Name, int Page);

public interface IUserService
{
    [Cache] Task<User> GetAsync(int id);                     // MyApp.IUserService.GetAsync:42
    [Cache] Task<List<User>> SearchAsync(UserQuery query);   // MyApp.IUserService.SearchAsync:(alice:2)
    [Cache] Task<List<User>> ByIdsAsync(int[] ids);          // MyApp.IUserService.ByIdsAsync:3f2a… (hashed)
}
```

## How arguments become keys

- **Simple values** (strings, numbers, `bool`, `Guid`, dates, enums) are written as they are: `GetAsync:42`.
- **Records, classes and structs** whose public properties and fields are simple values are written field by field:
  `SearchAsync:(alice:2)`. Two records with equal values give the same key.
- **Types that implement `ICacheKeyProvider`** contribute their `CacheKeyPart`.
- **Everything else**, such as arrays and collections, goes through the key generator. The default,
  `FastHashKeyGenerator`, hashes the arguments into a key such as `ByIdsAsync:11b474c4…`.
- A `CancellationToken` parameter is never part of the key.
- Keys don't depend on the current culture: `-1`, `1.5` and dates are written the same under every culture.

On .NET 9 and later the decorator writes simple keys into a stack buffer and looks them up without allocating.

## Types whose state is private

A type with only private state would give every value the same key, so the key generators refuse it with an
`InvalidOperationException` instead of returning wrong results. Implement `ICacheKeyProvider` on it:

```cs
public sealed class TenantId(Guid value) : ICacheKeyProvider
{
    private readonly Guid _value = value;   // private state: MethodCache can't see it

    public string CacheKeyPart => _value.ToString("N");
}
```

## Readable keys while debugging

`JsonKeyGenerator` writes the arguments it handles as JSON (for example `[42,"alice"]`) instead of a hash:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.Replace(ServiceDescriptor.Singleton<ICacheKeyGenerator, JsonKeyGenerator>());
```

The JSON is followed by a short hash of the arguments' runtime types (`[42,"alice"]:3f2a…`), so arguments that
write the same JSON, such as `1` and `1L` or two classes with the same properties, still get different keys.

Both generators are in `MethodCache.Extensibility`. Keys built by the decorator itself (simple values, records,
`ICacheKeyProvider`) don't change with the generator.

## Building a key yourself

`MethodCacheKeys` builds the same key the decorator uses, so you can invalidate or inspect one entry without guessing
the format:

```cs
var key = MethodCacheKeys.For(typeof(IOrderService), nameof(IOrderService.GetAsync), MethodCacheKeys.Part(42));
await cache.InvalidateByKeysAsync(key);   // "Docs.Invalidation.IOrderService.GetAsync:42"
```

## Things to know

- **Keys contain the arguments.** Don't cache methods that take secrets such as passwords or tokens as arguments; pass
  an identifier instead. Hashed keys are not encryption.
- **`Version` changes every key** of a method, so values cached by an earlier version are ignored. See
  [Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md#versions).
- To see the keys your application produces, list them with `ICacheAdministrator.ListEntries()` or the admin
  endpoints ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/expiration.md -->

# Expiration

Each cached method decides how long its entries live. The settings below can be set on `[Cache]`, in startup code, in
`appsettings.json` or at runtime ([Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md)).

```cs
public interface IReportService
{
    // Gone ten minutes after it was stored
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00")]
    Task<Report> GetAsync(int year);

    // Kept while it is read at least every five minutes, but never longer than an hour
    [Cache(Duration = "01:00:00", SlidingExpiration = "00:05:00")]
    Task<Session> GetSessionAsync(string id);

    // Reloaded in the background when it is read in its last minute, so callers never wait
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", RefreshAhead = "00:01:00")]
    Task<PriceList> GetPricesAsync(string region);

    // Changing the version changes every key, so values cached by the previous version are ignored
    [Cache(Duration = "1.00:00:00", Version = 2)]
    Task<Report> GetYearlyAsync(int year);
}
```

Time spans use the `TimeSpan` format: `"00:05:00"` is five minutes, `"01:00:00"` an hour, `"1.00:00:00"` a day. A
value that isn't a positive time span is a build error ([MC0004](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0004)).

## Duration

`Duration` is how long an entry lives after it was stored. A method without one uses the global default:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(config =>
    config.DefaultPolicy(o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15))));
```

Without any default, entries live for `MethodCacheMemoryOptions.DefaultExpiration` (five minutes). No entry lives
longer than `MethodCacheMemoryOptions.MaxExpiration` (seven days). See [Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md).

## Sliding expiration

`SlidingExpiration` keeps an entry while it is read: each read extends its life by the sliding window. It never lives
past its `Duration`; without a `Duration`, only `MaxExpiration` limits it.

## Refresh-ahead

`RefreshAhead` reloads an entry in the background when it is read within that window before it expires. The caller
gets the cached value at once, and the reload replaces it, so a popular entry never makes anyone wait. An entry that
isn't read in the window simply expires.

## Versions

`Version` is part of every key the method produces. Raise it when the shape of the cached result changes, for example
after adding a property, so values cached by the previous deployment are never returned. The old entries expire on
their own.

## Spreading out expiry

Entries created at the same moment, for example right after a deploy, also expire together.
`MethodCacheMemoryOptions.JitterMaxDuration` adds a random extra lifetime to each entry to spread them out
([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md)).

## Removing entries early

Expiration is for data that may be a little old. When you know data changed, remove it right away with
[invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/invalidation.md -->

# Invalidation

Expiration removes entries eventually; invalidation removes them the moment you know the data changed.

## Tags

Give cached methods tags, and list the same tags on the methods that change the data:

```cs
public interface IOrderService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["orders", "order:{orderId}"])]
    Task<Order> GetAsync(int orderId);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:05:00", Tags = ["orders", "customer:{customerId}:orders"])]
    Task<List<Order>> ListForCustomerAsync(int customerId);

    // Removes this order and the customer's list, nothing else
    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["order:{orderId}", "customer:{customerId}:orders"])]
    Task CancelAsync(int orderId, int customerId);

    // Removes every cached order
    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["orders"])]
    Task ImportAsync(Stream file);
}
```

- `[CacheInvalidate]` removes every entry with any of its tags once the method has completed successfully. If it
  throws, nothing is removed.
- A tag can be shared by many methods, so one write clears every cached view of the same data.
- `[CacheInvalidate]` without tags removes nothing and is reported as [MCG005](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg005).

## Tag templates

`"order:{orderId}"` is filled in from the method's arguments: `GetAsync(42)` is tagged `order:42`, and
`CancelAsync(42, 7)` removes `order:42`. The name in braces must be a parameter of the method it is on (case doesn't
matter); an unknown name is reported as [MCG009](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg009), with a code fix that offers the
closest parameter. An argument's text is inserted as it is, even if it contains braces: an id of `"{org}"` gives
the tag `order:{org}` on both the cached call and the invalidation.

A template takes a parameter name only. `"{order.Id}"` is not a template and stays literal text, so every call would
share one tag; it is reported as [MCG015](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg015). Add the id as a parameter, as `UpdateAsync(int id, Product product)` does in
[Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md).

## From code

`ICacheManager` invalidates by tag, by key or by pattern:

```cs
await cache.InvalidateByTagsAsync("order:42", "customer:7:orders");
```

```cs
var key = MethodCacheKeys.For(typeof(IOrderService), nameof(IOrderService.GetAsync), MethodCacheKeys.Part(42));
await cache.InvalidateByKeysAsync(key);   // "Docs.Invalidation.IOrderService.GetAsync:42"
```

```cs
await cache.InvalidateByTagPatternAsync("customer:7:*");   // in-memory cache only
```

- `MethodCacheKeys.For` builds the same key as the generated decorator ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md)).
- Patterns match tags, with `*` for any number of characters and `?` for one. With a distributed cache configured,
  `InvalidateByTagPatternAsync` throws `NotSupportedException`, because the distributed cache can't list its tags;
  invalidate exact tags instead.
- The admin endpoints and `ICacheAdministrator` also invalidate by tag ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).

## With several instances

With [Redis or SQL Server](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md), invalidating a tag or key removes it from the distributed cache and
tells every instance to drop its in-memory copy. You don't need to do anything else.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/fail-safe.md -->

# Fail-safe

Fail-safe keeps an expired value for a while and returns it when calling the method again fails, so a database or API
outage shows slightly old data instead of errors. It is off by default.

## Turning it on

For every cached method at once:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(config => config.FailSafe(
    duration: TimeSpan.FromHours(1),              // how long an expired value is kept as a fallback
    timeout: TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(200),      // optional: don't wait longer than this when a fallback exists
    retryAfter: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)));       // optional: reuse the fallback this long before trying again
```

or in `appsettings.json`:

```json
{
  "MethodCache": {
    "FailSafe": { "Duration": "01:00:00", "Timeout": "00:00:00.200", "RetryAfter": "00:00:30" }
  }
}
```

## What happens

- **When the method throws**, the caller gets the expired value if it is younger than `duration`. That value is then
  reused for `retryAfter` (default 30 seconds) before the method is called again, so a failing dependency isn't
  hammered.
- **When the method is slow** and `timeout` is set, the caller gets the expired value after `timeout` and the call
  finishes in the background; its result replaces the old value. Without an expired value the caller waits as usual.
- A caller's own cancellation is never treated as a failure, so it doesn't trigger fail-safe.
- Without an expired value, the exception reaches the caller as usual.

## Per method

A method or group can change any of it, and its own setting wins over the central one:

```cs
public interface IAccountService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:05:00", FailSafe = "01:00:00", FailSafeTimeout = "00:00:00.200")]
    Task<Rates> GetRatesAsync();

    [Cache(FailSafe = "off")]   // a balance must never be old, so an error is better
    Task<decimal> GetBalanceAsync(int accountId);
}
```

In code, use the same builder method: `Configure(o => o.FailSafe(TimeSpan.FromHours(1)))`. `o.FailSafe(TimeSpan.Zero)`
turns it off. In `appsettings.json`, a method takes `FailSafe` (a time span or `"off"`), `FailSafeTimeout` and
`FailSafeRetryAfter`.

## Limits

The fallback lives in each instance's memory, so right after a restart there is none until the method has succeeded
once.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/conditional-caching.md -->

# Conditional caching

Sometimes a result should be returned but not remembered: an empty search, a product that doesn't exist yet, a
response that says "try again later".

## CacheWhen

`CacheWhen` stores a result only when the predicate returns true:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(config =>
{
    // Don't remember empty search results: the next search asks the database again
    config.ForService<IProductService>()
          .Method(s => s.SearchAsync(Any<string>.Value))
          .CacheWhen(results => results.Count > 0);

    // A product that doesn't exist yet may be created any moment
    config.ForService<IProductService>()
          .Method(s => s.FindAsync(Any<int>.Value))
          .CacheWhen(product => product is not null);
});
```

- A rejected result is still returned to the caller, and the next call runs the method again.
- The entry it would have replaced, including a fail-safe value, stays.
- The predicate runs once per load, never on a cache hit. If it throws, the result is returned and not stored.
- It is set in startup code only, so it can't come from `appsettings.json`. `Any<T>.Value` stands for any argument.

To stop caching `null` everywhere, set `CacheNullValues = false` on the [memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md) instead.

## Skipping the cache for one call

With [manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md), `When` decides per call whether to use the cache at all:

```cs
var results = await cache.GetOrCreateAsync(
    $"search:{text}",
    async (ctx, ct) => await search(),
    o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10))
          .When(ctx => !preview));   // preview requests skip the cache entirely
```

When the predicate returns false, the factory runs and its result is neither read from nor written to the cache.
`When`, `OnHit`, `OnMiss` and `WithMetrics` only apply to `GetOrCreateAsync`; configuring them for a `[Cache]`
method throws `InvalidOperationException` at startup instead of being silently ignored.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/configuration.md -->

# Configuration

A cached method's policy (duration, sliding expiration, refresh-ahead, fail-safe, tags, group, version) can come from
four layers. Change it in `appsettings.json` or at runtime, and the next call uses it, without a redeploy.

| Layer | How you set it | Priority | Changes while running |
|-------|----------------|----------|-----------------------|
| Attributes | `[Cache(...)]` on the interface method | 10 (lowest) | No |
| Startup code | `AddMethodCache(config => ...)` | 40 | No |
| Configuration | `AddMethodCacheFromConfiguration(configuration)` | 50 | Yes, when the configuration reloads |
| Runtime overrides | `IRuntimeCacheConfigurator` | 100 (highest) | Yes |

When several layers configure the same method, they are merged setting by setting, and the highest layer that sets a
setting wins. A runtime override of `Duration` leaves the attribute's `Tags` in place.

## Defaults and groups

Within the layers, each setting comes from the most specific place that sets it: the method itself, then its group,
then the defaults.

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(config =>
{
    // Every cached method: fills in what the method leaves unset
    config.DefaultPolicy(o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15)));

    // Methods in the "user-data" group: [Cache("user-data")] or WithGroup("user-data")
    config.ForGroup("user-data")
          .Configure(o => o.WithSlidingExpiration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10)));

    // One method
    config.ForService<IUserService>()
          .Method(s => s.GetProfileAsync(Any<int>.Value))
          .Configure(o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromHours(2)).RefreshAhead(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)));
});
```

- `DefaultPolicy` applies to every cached method, also ones that only have `[Cache]`. `[Cache(Duration = "00:10:00")]`
  keeps its ten minutes while the defaults fill in what it leaves out.
- A method joins a group with `[Cache("name")]`, `WithGroup("name")` in code, or `Group` in `appsettings.json`.
- `Any<T>.Value` stands for any argument when you point at a method.

## appsettings.json

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheFromConfiguration(builder.Configuration);   // the "MethodCache" section
```

```json
{
  "MethodCache": {
    "Defaults": { "Duration": "00:15:00" },
    "FailSafe": { "Duration": "01:00:00" },
    "Services": {
      "MyApp.IUserService.GetProfileAsync": {
        "Duration": "01:00:00",
        "SlidingExpiration": "00:10:00",
        "RefreshAhead": "00:05:00",
        "Tags": ["users"],
        "Version": 1,
        "Notes": "Profiles change rarely"
      },
      "MyApp.IAccountService.GetBalanceAsync": { "FailSafe": "off" }
    }
  }
}
```

- Each key under `Services` is the **method id**: the full name of the interface, a dot and the method name. A generic
  interface is written with its type parameters (`MyApp.IRepository<T>.GetAsync`), and an overloaded method adds its
  parameter types (`MyApp.IUserService.FindAsync(int)`). The admin endpoints list every method id
  ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).
- Settings: `Duration`, `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead`, `FailSafe` (a time span or `"off"`), `FailSafeTimeout`,
  `FailSafeRetryAfter`, `Tags`, `Version`, `Group`, `Metadata` and `Notes`. `Metadata` and `Notes` are recorded for
  diagnostics and don't change caching.
- `Defaults` applies to every cached method; the top-level `FailSafe` section is described in [Fail-safe](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/fail-safe.md).
- Pass a section name as the second argument to read another section. Environment files such as
  `appsettings.Production.json` work as usual.
- Changes apply while the application runs, as soon as the configuration reloads (`appsettings.json` reloads on save
  by default).
- Only methods with `[Cache]` (or listed in `[assembly: CacheInterface]`) have a decorator, so the file can change
  their policy but can't make other methods cached. A method id that matches no cached method, such as a misspelled
  name, is logged as a warning at startup.
- An invalid value, such as a `Duration` that isn't a positive time span, makes `AddMethodCacheFromConfiguration`
  throw at startup. If a reloaded file has one, the reload is logged as an error and the previous policies stay.

## Runtime overrides

Runtime overrides win over everything else. Use them to change a policy without a deploy, for example to shorten a
duration during an incident:

```cs
var configurator = app.Services.GetRequiredService<IRuntimeCacheConfigurator>();

// One method, strongly typed, with who and why for the audit trail
await configurator.UpsertAsync<IOrdersService, Order>(
    s => s.GetAsync(Any<int>.Value),
    o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2)),
    new RuntimeOverrideMetadata(Owner: "ops", Reason: "Incident 4211", ExpiresAt: DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddHours(4)));

// By method id, for example from an admin form
await configurator.UpsertAsync("Docs.Configuration.IUserService.GetProfileAsync",
    o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10)));

// Back to the lower layers
await configurator.RemoveAsync<IOrdersService, Order>(s => s.GetAsync(Any<int>.Value));
await configurator.ClearAsync();
```

| Method | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `UpsertAsync` | Adds or replaces the override for one method, by expression or method id |
| `UpsertBatchAsync` | Several overrides in one call |
| `ApplyAsync` | Overrides for the methods listed with `ForService<T>().Method(...)`, as in startup code |
| `RemoveAsync` / `ClearAsync` | Removes one override, or all of them |
| `GetOverridesAsync` / `GetOverrideAsync` | Returns the active overrides |
| `WatchAsync` | Streams override changes |

- `RuntimeOverrideMetadata` (owner, reason, ticket, expiry) is kept with the override for auditing. An override stops
  applying when its `ExpiresAt` passes.
- Overrides are held in memory. They are lost on restart and not shared between instances.
- An override can't turn caching off: `WithDuration` requires a positive duration. To get rid of stale data,
  [invalidate](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md) it.

## Seeing the effective policy

`PolicyDiagnosticsService` (in `MethodCache.Policies`) shows each method's merged policy and which layers contributed:

```cs
var diagnostics = app.Services.GetRequiredService<PolicyDiagnosticsService>();

foreach (var report in diagnostics.GetAllPolicies())
{
    var sources = string.Join(", ", report.Contributions.Select(c => c.SourceId).Distinct());
    Console.WriteLine($"{report.MethodId}: Duration={report.Policy.Duration}, from {sources}");
}
```

`GetPolicy(methodId)` returns one method's report, and `FindBySource(sourceId)` the methods a layer configured. The
source ids are `attributes`, `startup-fluent`, `configuration-files` and `runtime-overrides`. The admin endpoint
`GET /methodcache/methods` shows the same ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).

## Validation

| Setting | Rule | Checked |
|---------|------|---------|
| `Duration`, `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead` | A positive time span | `[Cache]`: at build time ([MC0004](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0004)). Code: `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. JSON: at startup |
| `Version` | Zero or more | Code: `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. JSON: at startup |

`OnHit`, `OnMiss`, `WithMetrics` and `When` only apply to [manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md); configuring them for a
cached method throws `InvalidOperationException` at startup.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/manual-caching.md -->

# Manual caching

When an attribute doesn't fit, such as a call in the middle of a method or a client without an interface, use the same
cache through `ICacheManager` with a key you choose:

```cs
public sealed class OrderReader(ICacheManager cache, IOrderRepository orders)
{
    public ValueTask<Order> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) =>
        cache.GetOrCreateAsync(
            $"order:{id}",
            async (ctx, token) => await orders.GetAsync(id, token),
            o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30)).WithTags("orders", $"order:{id}"),
            cancellationToken: ct);
}
```

It shares the in-memory cache, the distributed cache, stampede protection and invalidation with `[Cache]` methods.

## Keys

You always pass the key yourself. MethodCache doesn't derive keys from the lambda, so a captured variable never ends
up in a key by accident, and two calls share an entry only when their keys are equal. Use a prefix per kind of data,
such as `order:42`, so keys from different places can't collide. An empty or whitespace key throws
`ArgumentException`.

## Options

`GetOrCreateAsync` takes every option, including callbacks and a predicate that only make sense per call:

```cs
var list = await cache.GetOrCreateAsync(
    $"orders:{customerId}:{status}",
    async (ctx, ct) => await orders.ListAsync(customerId, status, ct),
    o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30))
          .WithSlidingExpiration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10))
          .RefreshAhead(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5))
          .WithTags("orders", $"customer:{customerId}")
          .WithVersion(2)
          .OnHit(ctx => logger.LogDebug("Cache hit: {Key}", ctx.Key))
          .OnMiss(ctx => logger.LogDebug("Cache miss: {Key}", ctx.Key))
          .When(ctx => customerId > 0));   // skip the cache when false
```

- Duration, sliding expiration, refresh-ahead, tags and version work as described in [Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md) and
  [Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md).
- `When` skips the cache for this call when it returns false ([Conditional caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md)).
- `OnHit`, `OnMiss` and `WithMetrics` observe this call. The `CacheContext` they get carries the key and an `Items`
  dictionary scoped to the call.
- These policies live in code: `appsettings.json` and runtime overrides apply to `[Cache]` methods only.

## Reading without loading

```cs
var lookup = await cache.TryGetAsync<Order>("order:42");
if (lookup.Found)
{
    Console.WriteLine(lookup.Value);
}
```

`TryGetAsync` takes the same `version` an entry was stored with.

## Many keys at once

`GetOrCreateManyAsync` looks up every key and calls the factory once, with only the keys that were missing:

```cs
var users = await cache.GetOrCreateManyAsync<User>(
    userIds.Select(id => $"user:{id}"),
    async (missingKeys, ctx, ct) =>
    {
        var ids = missingKeys.Select(k => int.Parse(k["user:".Length..])).ToList();
        var loaded = await repository.GetUsersAsync(ids, ct);   // one query for all misses
        return loaded.ToDictionary(u => $"user:{u.Id}", u => u);
    },
    o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromHours(1)));
```

## Things to know

- Concurrent calls for the same key share one factory run. A caller's `cancellationToken` stops its own wait; if it
  cancels a run others joined, they run the factory again rather than fail.
- To cache a sequence, materialize it in the factory (`await query.ToListAsync(ct)`) and cache the list.
- `GetOrCreateAsync` is an extension method, so mocking libraries can't intercept it. In tests, pass a
  `NoOpCacheManager` ([Testing](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/testing.md)).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/third-party.md -->

# Caching third-party code

MethodCache can cache calls to code you don't own, such as API clients, cloud SDKs or payment gateways, to cut API
costs and latency. Pick one of three approaches:

| Approach | Best for |
|----------|----------|
| `[assembly: CacheInterface]` | A client that ships an interface: cache chosen methods with one line, no wrapper |
| A wrapper interface with `[Cache]` | A client without an interface (a sealed class or static methods) |
| `ICacheManager.GetOrCreateAsync` | One or two calls, or keys you want to build yourself |

## The client's own interface

Name the interface and the methods to cache in an assembly attribute, anywhere in your project:

```cs
[assembly: CacheInterface(typeof(IFxRatesClient), nameof(IFxRatesClient.GetRateAsync),
    Duration = "00:01:00", Tags = ["fx", "fx:{from}"])]
```

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IFxRatesClient, FxRatesClient>();   // the vendor's client, registered as usual
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
```

- The listed methods behave like methods with `[Cache]`: keys from the arguments, tag templates with the method's
  parameter names, zero-allocation hits on .NET 9 and later. Methods you don't list always reach the client, so writes
  are never cached by accident.
- The attribute's settings (`Duration`, `Tags`, `Group`, `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead`, `Version`) apply to
  every listed method. Give one method its own settings like any cached method:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(config => config
    .ForService<IFxRatesClient>()
    .Method(c => c.GetRateAsync(Any<string>.Value, Any<string>.Value))
    .Configure(o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30))));
```

- The method id in `appsettings.json` and the admin endpoints is the interface's full name, a dot and the method name,
  for example `FxVendor.IFxRatesClient.GetRateAsync`.
- List each interface once. It must be non-generic and come from another assembly; for your own interfaces, put
  `[Cache]` on the methods. A method with overloads can't be listed yet.
- Mistakes are build errors: [MCG010](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg010) (a type it can't cache),
  [MCG011](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg011) (a missing, overloaded or result-less method) and
  [MCG012](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg012) (an interface listed twice).

## A wrapper interface

Define an interface in your project with the calls you need, and put the settings on it:

```cs
public interface IRates
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:01:00", Tags = ["fx", "fx:{from}"])]
    Task<decimal> GetAsync(string from, string to);
}

public sealed class Rates(FxRatesClient client) : IRates   // calls the vendor's concrete class
{
    public Task<decimal> GetAsync(string from, string to) => client.GetRateAsync(from, to);
}
```

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<FxRatesClient>();
builder.Services.AddScoped<IRates, Rates>();
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
```

Static methods and sealed classes work the same way: the wrapper calls them, and the interface carries the attributes.

## An explicit key

```cs
var rate = await cache.GetOrCreateAsync(
    $"fx:{from}:{to}",
    async (ctx, ct) => await client.GetRateAsync(from, to),
    o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1)).WithTags("fx"));
```

See [Manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md).

## Things to know

- **Leave writes uncached.** Payments, uploads and deletes must not be cached; mark wrapper methods that change data
  with `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]`.
- **Exceptions are not cached.** With [fail-safe](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/fail-safe.md) on, the previous value is served while the client
  fails.
- **Invalidate from a webhook** with `cache.InvalidateByTagsAsync("fx:EUR")` when the vendor tells you data changed.
- **Share results between instances** with a [distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md) when every instance calls the
  same paid API.
- **Start with short durations** and lengthen them once you know how fresh the data must be.


---

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.HttpCaching/README.md -->

# MethodCache.HttpCaching

HTTP caching for `HttpClient`, the way a browser does it: responses are cached according to `Cache-Control`,
revalidated with `ETag` / `Last-Modified`, and a `304 Not Modified` comes back to your code as the full cached
response. It follows RFC 9111.

```cs
builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IGitHubClient, GitHubClient>()
    .AddHttpCaching();
```

That is all. Your typed client keeps calling `GetAsync` as before.

## What it does

| The server sends | What happens on the next request |
|---|---|
| `Cache-Control: max-age=60` | Served from cache for 60 seconds, no network call |
| `ETag: "abc"` (or `Last-Modified`) | Sent with `If-None-Match: "abc"`; a 304 is answered from the cache |
| both | Served from cache while fresh, then revalidated with the ETag |
| `Vary: Accept-Language` | One cached response per language |
| `no-store` | Never cached |

- A successful `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` removes the cached responses for that URL (and for same-origin
  `Location` / `Content-Location`) for every caller, language and key header value, so nobody reads stale data
  after a write.
- Cached responses carry an `Age` header, as the standard requires.
- Each HttpClient has its own settings and its own entries.
- Request directives are honored: `no-cache` (revalidates and stores the answer), `no-store`, `max-age`, `max-stale`, `min-fresh` and `only-if-cached`.
- `Range` requests go to the origin, and `206 Partial Content` is never stored.
- Requests that carry their own `If-None-Match` or `If-Modified-Since` go to the origin, so your `304` reaches you.
- Statuses that are cacheable by default (`200`, `203`, `204`, `301`, `404`, ...) are stored; other `2xx` responses only when they say how long they stay fresh (`max-age` or `Expires`).

## Settings

Settings are per HttpClient:

```cs
builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IWeatherClient, WeatherClient>()
    .AddHttpCaching(options =>
    {
        options.EnableStaleIfError = true;           // serve the last response when the API is down
        options.EnableStaleWhileRevalidate = true;   // when the server sends stale-while-revalidate
        options.AddDiagnosticHeaders = true;         // X-Cache: HIT / MISS / REVALIDATED / STALE
    });
```

| Option | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `IsSharedCache` | `false` | `false`: a private cache; `Authorization` and `Cookie` are part of the key so callers never see each other's responses. `true`: a shared cache; `private` and authorized responses are not stored, `s-maxage` applies |
| `DefaultMaxAge` | `null` | Freshness for a response with only an `ETag`/`Last-Modified`. `null` revalidates every time |
| `AllowHeuristicFreshness` | `true` | 10% of the time since `Last-Modified`, at most `MaxHeuristicFreshness` (1 hour) |
| `StaleRetention` | 24 hours | How long a stale entry is kept for revalidation and the stale options below |
| `EnableStaleWhileRevalidate` | `false` | Serve stale at once and refresh in the background, within the server's `stale-while-revalidate` |
| `EnableStaleIfError` | `false` | Serve stale when the request fails or returns 5xx, within `stale-if-error` or `MaxStaleIfError` (24 hours) |
| `MaxResponseSize` | 10 MB | Larger responses are not cached. A body without `Content-Length` is read up to this size, then streamed to the caller uncached |
| `KeyHeaders` | empty | Request headers that are always part of the key, for APIs that vary on a header without sending `Vary` |
| `CacheableMethods` | GET, HEAD | POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE are never cached, even if added. |
| `AddDiagnosticHeaders` | `false` | Adds `X-Cache`, `X-Cache-Age` and `X-Cache-TTL` |

`must-revalidate` (and `proxy-revalidate` / `s-maxage` in a shared cache) always wins: such responses are never
served stale.

## Storage

Responses are kept in memory, in a cache of their own (your app's `IMemoryCache` is not touched). The total size
is shared by all clients:

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<HttpCacheStorageOptions>(o => o.MaxCacheSize = 50 * 1024 * 1024); // default 100 MB
```

### Sharing responses between instances

With several instances of your app, each one would otherwise fetch and revalidate on its own. Turn on
`UseDistributedCache` and responses are kept in the registered `IDistributedCache` instead of memory, the same
Redis or SQL Server that MethodCache uses:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis("localhost:6379");
builder.Services.Configure<HttpCacheStorageOptions>(o => o.UseDistributedCache = true);
```

Now an ETag fetched by one instance is revalidated (and usually answered with a 304) by all of them, and a POST
through one instance invalidates the cached GET for all of them. If the distributed cache is down, requests go
straight to the origin. Apps that share one Redis or SQL Server should each set their own `KeyPrefix`
(default `methodcache-http:`). `ClearAsync()` cannot clear a distributed cache; entries there expire on their own.

To store responses somewhere else entirely, register your own `IHttpCacheStorage` before `AddHttpCaching()`.

### Time

Freshness, eviction from the memory store and the background revalidation timeout all read the time from the
`TimeProvider` registered in the container, if there is one. Register a fake `TimeProvider`, for example from
`Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`, to test expiry without waiting.

## Metrics

Every request is counted on the `MethodCache` meter, so `AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()` from
MethodCache.OpenTelemetry (or `AddMeter("MethodCache")`) picks them up:

| Instrument | Tags |
|---|---|
| `methodcache.http.requests_total` | `client`, `outcome` (`hit`, `miss`, `revalidated`, `stale`, `bypass`, `error` when the request threw) |
| `methodcache.http.request_duration` (ms) | `client`, `outcome` |


---

<!-- source: docs/features/distributed-cache.md -->

# Distributed cache

By default each application instance has its own in-memory cache. Add a distributed cache to share results between
instances and keep them across restarts:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis("localhost:6379");   // MethodCache.Redis
```

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheSqlServer(connectionString);   // MethodCache.SqlServer
```

## How it works

- Results live in memory (L1) and in the distributed cache (L2). An in-memory miss reads the distributed cache before
  running your method, and a new result is written to both.
- Invalidating a key or tag removes it from the distributed cache, and a backplane tells every other instance to drop
  its in-memory copy at once: Redis pub/sub, or a table that SQL Server instances poll.
- `[Cache]` methods and `GetOrCreateAsync` need no changes.
- MethodCache keeps its own distributed cache and connection, so your application's `IDistributedCache` is left alone.

## When the distributed cache is down

Calls keep working from memory and your methods; the distributed cache never fails or stalls a call. Each call to it
is capped at one second, a circuit breaker skips it until it is back, and invalidations are queued and retried
instead of throwing. Until they are stored, the instance doesn't read entries from it, so an invalidated value can't
come back. The [health check](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md#health-check) reports Degraded while this lasts.

## Serialization

Values are written as JSON with System.Text.Json. The `MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack` package makes them
smaller and faster to read:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis("localhost:6379");
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheMessagePack();   // MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack
```

Each entry records its format, so after a switch older entries count as misses. Under Native AOT, register your
`JsonSerializerContext` ([Native AOT](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/native-aot.md)).

## Any IDistributedCache

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheDistributedCache(
    _ => new MemoryDistributedCache(Options.Create(new MemoryDistributedCacheOptions())));   // any IDistributedCache
```

Without a backplane, other instances keep their in-memory copy of an invalidated entry until it expires. Register an
`IBackplane` (in `MethodCache.Extensibility`) to send invalidations to them.

## Limits

- Pattern invalidation (`InvalidateByTagPatternAsync`) throws `NotSupportedException` with a distributed cache.
- [Fail-safe](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/fail-safe.md) values and [runtime overrides](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md#runtime-overrides) live in each instance's
  memory.

## Package guides

The [Redis](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.Redis/README.md) and [SQL Server](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.SqlServer/README.md) READMEs
cover their options, shared connections, table creation and outage settings.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/monitoring.md -->

# Monitoring

MethodCache shows what it is doing in code, over HTTP, in health checks and through OpenTelemetry.

## In code

`ICacheAdministrator`, registered by `AddMethodCache()`, reads statistics, lists methods and entries, and invalidates:

```cs
var stats = await admin.GetStatsAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Hit ratio {stats.HitRatio:P0}, {stats.Entries} entries");

foreach (var method in admin.GetMethods())
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{method.MethodId}: {method.Duration}");
}

var entries = admin.ListEntries(tag: "user:42");
await admin.InvalidateTagsAsync(["user:42"]);
```

- `GetStatsAsync()`: hits, misses, hit ratio, evictions, entries and estimated memory.
- `GetMethods()`: every cached method with its method id and effective policy.
- `ListEntries(keyPrefix, tag, limit)` and `GetEntry(key)`: live entries, without their values.
- `InvalidateTagsAsync(tags)`, `RemoveEntryAsync(key)` and `ClearAsync()`.

It works with the default in-memory cache manager; a custom `ICacheManager` has no administrator.

## Admin endpoints

The `MethodCache.AspNetCore` package exposes the same operations over HTTP, behind an authorization policy you choose:

```cs
builder.Services.AddScoped<IUserService, UserService>();
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddAuthorization(o => o.AddPolicy("CacheAdmins", p => p.RequireRole("Admin")));

var app = builder.Build();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapMethodCacheAdmin("CacheAdmins");
app.MapHealthChecks("/health");
```

`GET /methodcache/stats`, `/methods`, `/entries` and `/entry`, `POST /methodcache/invalidate` and `DELETE` for entries.
The [package README](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.AspNetCore/README.md) lists every endpoint. They don't change policies;
use [runtime overrides](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md#runtime-overrides) for that.

## Health check

`AddHealthChecks().AddMethodCache()` reports Healthy when the cache answers, with `entries`, `hitRatio`, `evictions`
and `memoryUsageBytes` in the report data. With Redis or SQL Server it reports Degraded while that cache is
unreachable and MethodCache serves from memory only.

## OpenTelemetry

The `MethodCache.OpenTelemetry` package records metrics for every call (hits, misses, errors and load time per
method, and the size of the in-memory cache) and spans for misses and invalidations:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheOpenTelemetry(); // after AddMethodCache, which registers the cache it instruments

builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
    .WithTracing(tracing => tracing
        .AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()
        .AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()
        .AddOtlpExporter())
    .WithMetrics(metrics => metrics
        .AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()
        .AddOtlpExporter());
```

Hits have no span, so they stay allocation-free, but they are counted. Cache keys are left off spans unless you turn
on `RecordCacheKeys`, because keys can contain argument values. See the
[package README](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.OpenTelemetry/README.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/memory-cache.md -->

# Memory cache

The in-memory cache is a W-TinyLFU cache: when it is full, it keeps the entries that are read often and evicts the
rest, so a burst of one-off reads doesn't push out your hot data. Configure it with `MethodCacheMemoryOptions`:

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<MethodCacheMemoryOptions>(o =>
{
    o.MaxItems = 50_000;                              // default 10,000
    o.DefaultExpiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10);   // for methods without a Duration; default 5 minutes
    o.JitterMaxDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);   // spread out entries created together
    o.CacheNullValues = false;                        // a null result means "try again next time"
});
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|--------|---------|--------------|
| `MaxItems` | 10,000 | The most entries kept |
| `MaxMemoryBytes` | | The most total weight kept when a `Weigher` is set |
| `Weigher` | none | Returns an entry's cost, for example its size in bytes |
| `DefaultExpiration` | 5 minutes | The duration of methods with none of their own and no `DefaultPolicy` |
| `MaxExpiration` | 7 days | No entry lives longer, whatever its duration |
| `JitterMaxDuration` | zero | Adds a random extra lifetime up to this value, so entries created together don't expire together |
| `CacheNullValues` | `true` | Caches `null` results like any other value |
| `EnableStatistics` | `true` | Counts hits, misses and evictions for the [statistics](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md) |

## Bounding by size

Object sizes can't be measured reliably at runtime, so to bound the cache by memory you say what an entry costs:

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<MethodCacheMemoryOptions>(o =>
{
    o.MaxMemoryBytes = 256 * 1024 * 1024;   // bound the cache by size instead of by count
    o.Weigher = (key, value) => value is string s ? s.Length * 2 : 64;
});
```

The weigher must be fast, thread-safe and return a non-negative value. Without one, `MaxMemoryBytes` is ignored.

## Null values

`null` results are cached by default, so a method that returns `null` isn't run again on every call. Set
`CacheNullValues = false` when `null` means "not there yet" and the next call should try again, or use
[`CacheWhen`](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md) for one method.

## Cached objects are shared

The cache stores the object your method returned and hands the same instance to every caller. Don't change a cached
object; return immutable types such as records, or copies.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/native-aot.md -->

# Native AOT

MethodCache works in Native AOT and trimmed applications. The source generator writes the decorators, their
registration and the cache keys at build time, so nothing is found or built with reflection at runtime. CI publishes a
test application with Native AOT on every change and checks that caching, the automatic registration and
`[assembly: CacheInterface]` work.

## In-memory caching

Nothing to do: the in-memory cache stores your objects as they are, without serializing them.

## Distributed caching

Values written to Redis or SQL Server are serialized with System.Text.Json. Under Native AOT it needs a
`JsonSerializerContext` that lists every type your cached methods return:

```cs
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Product))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(List<Product>))]   // every type a cached method returns
public sealed partial class ShopJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext;
```

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis("localhost:6379");
builder.Services.AddSingleton<ISerializer>(new JsonCacheSerializer(ShopJsonContext.Default.Options));
```

`ISerializer` and `JsonCacheSerializer` are in `MethodCache.Extensibility`. MethodCache can't generate this context
for you, because one source generator can't see another generator's output.

## Keys

Keys built by the decorator (simple values, records, `ICacheKeyProvider`) need no reflection. Arguments that go
through the key generator, such as collections, are hashed by `FastHashKeyGenerator`. See [Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/testing.md -->

# Testing

## Testing your service

The implementation of a cached interface is a plain class: create it directly in unit tests and no caching is
involved.

## Testing with caching

To test the caching itself, such as invalidation tags, build a service provider the way the application does:

```cs
var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddSingleton<Database>();
services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();
services.AddMethodCache();
var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider();

// Resolved through the generated decorator, exactly as in the application
var products = provider.CreateScope().ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IProductService>();
```

`ICacheAdministrator` from the same provider lists the entries and their keys, which helps when a test needs to check
what was cached ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).

## Turning caching off

Register `NoOpCacheManager` after `AddMethodCache()` and every call reaches your implementation:

```cs
var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddSingleton<Database>();
services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();
services.AddMethodCache();
services.AddSingleton<ICacheManager, NoOpCacheManager>();   // after AddMethodCache: every call reaches ProductService
```

For code that uses [manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md), pass a `NoOpCacheManager` directly. `GetOrCreateAsync` is an
extension method, so mocking libraries can't intercept it:

```cs
ICacheManager cache = new NoOpCacheManager();   // never caches: the factory runs on every call
var reader = new OrderReader(cache, repository);
```

`NoOpCacheManager` is in `MethodCache.Extensibility`.

## Time

The cache reads the time from the `TimeProvider` registered in the container, if there is one. Register a fake
`TimeProvider`, for example from `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`, to test expiration without waiting.
This includes the background cleanup of the memory cache and, with `MethodCache.HttpCaching`, response freshness,
eviction and the background revalidation timeout.


---

<!-- source: docs/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

To see what is actually cached, list the entries with `ICacheAdministrator.ListEntries()` or `GET /methodcache/entries`,
and the effective policy of every method with `GetMethods()` or `GET /methodcache/methods` ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).

## The method runs on every call

- **The attribute is on the class.** `[Cache]` is read from the interface only. The analyzer reports
  [MC0001](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0001) and its code fix moves the attribute.
- **The service was registered after `AddMethodCache()`.** Call `AddMethodCache()` after your own registrations.
- **The caller doesn't use the interface.** The cache is a decorator around the interface. Resolving or injecting the
  class itself, or calling the method from inside the class (`this.GetAsync(...)`), skips it.
- **The arguments differ between calls.** A `DateTime.Now`, a new `Guid` or a request object with a unique id in it
  makes every key different. List the keys to check ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md)).
- **The result is not stored on purpose:** a `CacheWhen` predicate rejected it, the result is `null` with
  `CacheNullValues = false`, or the call threw. Exceptions are never cached.
- **A test registered `NoOpCacheManager`**, which never caches ([Testing](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/testing.md)).

## Old data after an update

- **The tags don't match.** `[CacheInvalidate]` removes only the tags it lists. Compare them with the cached methods'
  tags.
- **A tag template isn't filled in.** The name in braces must be a parameter of that method:
  [MCG009](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg009) warns about unknown names. A property path such as `"{product.Id}"` is
  not a template and stays literal ([MCG015](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg015)); pass the id as a parameter.
- **The update method threw.** Invalidation runs only after the method completes successfully.
- **The data changed outside the interface**, for example in another service or a database job. Invalidate from that
  code with `ICacheManager.InvalidateByTagsAsync` ([Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md#from-code)).
- **You run several instances** with only the in-memory cache. Each instance has its own cache; add
  [Redis or SQL Server](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md) so invalidations reach all of them. With a custom
  `IDistributedCache`, also register an `IBackplane`.
- **Fail-safe returned an expired value** because the method failed ([Fail-safe](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/fail-safe.md)).

## A change in appsettings.json has no effect

- `AddMethodCacheFromConfiguration(builder.Configuration)` must be called.
- The key under `Services` must be the method id: the interface's full name, a dot and the method name. An unknown id
  is logged as a warning at startup. `GET /methodcache/methods` lists the ids.
- A runtime override for the method wins over the file ([Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md)).
- An invalid value in a reloaded file is logged as an error, and the previous policies stay.

## Exceptions

| Exception | Cause |
|-----------|-------|
| `InvalidOperationException` when building a key | An argument type has only private state, so every value would get the same key. Implement `ICacheKeyProvider` ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#types-whose-state-is-private)) |
| `InvalidOperationException` at startup | `OnHit`, `OnMiss`, `WithMetrics` or `When` configured for a `[Cache]` method. They apply to `GetOrCreateAsync` only |
| `NotSupportedException` from `InvalidateByTagPatternAsync` | Pattern invalidation doesn't work with a distributed cache. Invalidate exact tags |
| `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` from `WithDuration` | Durations must be positive. An override can't turn caching off; invalidate instead |
| An exception from `AddMethodCacheFromConfiguration` | An invalid value in the `MethodCache` section at startup |

## A caller changed a cached object, and others see the change

The cache hands the same instance to every caller. Return immutable types such as records, or copies
([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md#cached-objects-are-shared)).

## Build errors and warnings

Every `MC` and `MCG` diagnostic, with what to do about it, is in [Build diagnostics](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md -->

# Build Diagnostics

MethodCache checks your attributes when you build. Errors mean the method would not be cached as written, so the
build stops; warnings point at attributes that do nothing. Every diagnostic links to its section below, and the ones
marked **Code fix** can be fixed from the light bulb in Visual Studio, Rider or VS Code.

| Id | Severity | Summary | Code fix |
|----|----------|---------|----------|
| [MC0001](#mc0001) | Warning | `[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` on a class member | Move to the interface |
| [MC0004](#mc0004) | Error | A time span that is not a positive `TimeSpan` | |
| [MCG001](#mcg001) | Error | `[Cache]` on a `void` method | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG002](#mcg002) | Error | `[Cache]` on `Task`/`ValueTask` without a result | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG003](#mcg003) | Error | `[Cache]` with `ref`, `out` or `in` parameters | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG004](#mcg004) | Error | `[Cache]` and `[CacheInvalidate]` on the same method | |
| [MCG005](#mcg005) | Warning | `[CacheInvalidate]` without tags | |
| [MCG006](#mcg006) | Error | `[Cache]` with a pointer parameter | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG007](#mcg007) | Error | `[Cache]` with a `Span<T>` or other ref struct parameter | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG009](#mcg009) | Warning | A tag names a parameter the method does not have | Use the closest parameter |
| [MCG010](#mcg010) | Error | `[assembly: CacheInterface]` names a type it can't decorate | |
| [MCG011](#mcg011) | Error | `[assembly: CacheInterface]` lists a method it can't cache | |
| [MCG012](#mcg012) | Error | The same interface in more than one `[assembly: CacheInterface]` | |
| [MCG013](#mcg013) | Error | An interface with static abstract members | |
| [MCG014](#mcg014) | Error | `[Cache]` on a lazy sequence | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG015](#mcg015) | Warning | A tag placeholder that is not a parameter name, such as `{product.Id}` | |

## MC0001

`[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` is on a class, struct or record member. MethodCache generates a decorator for the
interface, so it only reads attributes on interface methods, and this one is ignored.

```csharp
public interface IUserService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:05:00")]      // here
    Task<User> GetAsync(int id);
}

public class UserService : IUserService
{
    public Task<User> GetAsync(int id) => ...;   // not here
}
```

**Code fix:** moves the attribute to the interface method the member implements (adding the `using` if needed), or
removes it when the member implements no interface. To cache an interface you don't own, see the
[third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MC0004

`Duration`, `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead`, `FailSafe` or `FailSafeTimeout` on `[Cache]` or
`[assembly: CacheInterface]` is not a positive time span. Use the `TimeSpan` format: `"00:05:00"` (five minutes),
`"01:00:00"` (an hour) or `"1.00:00:00"` (a day). `FailSafe` also accepts `"off"`.

## MCG001

`[Cache]` on a `void` method: there is no result to cache. Return the value, or remove `[Cache]`. If the method
changes data, you probably want `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` instead.

## MCG002

`[Cache]` on a method returning `Task` or `ValueTask` without a result. Return `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>`, or remove
`[Cache]`. A write method usually wants `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` instead.

## MCG003

`[Cache]` on a method with `ref`, `out` or `in` parameters. Those can't be part of a cache key, and a cached call
could not set an `out` value. Pass the values by value and return them, for example as a record.

## MCG004

`[Cache]` and `[CacheInvalidate]` on the same method. A method either reads (cached) or writes (invalidates); keep
the one that matches what it does.

## MCG005

`[CacheInvalidate]` without tags removes nothing. List the tags of the cached methods it should clear:

```csharp
[Cache(Tags = new[] { "users", "user:{id}" })]
Task<User> GetAsync(int id);

[CacheInvalidate(Tags = new[] { "users", "user:{id}" })]
Task UpdateAsync(int id, User user);
```

## MCG006

`[Cache]` on a method with a pointer parameter. Pointers can't be part of a cache key; pass a value or an array.

## MCG007

`[Cache]` on a method with a `Span<T>`, `ReadOnlySpan<T>` or other ref struct parameter. They can't be stored in a
cache key; pass an array, `Memory<T>` or a string.

## MCG009

A tag such as `"user:{userId}"` names a parameter the method does not have, so the braces stay literal text and every
call shares that tag. The name between the braces must match a parameter name (case doesn't matter).

A template takes a parameter name only; a property path such as `"{product.Id}"` is reported as [MCG015](#mcg015).

**Code fix:** offers the closest parameter names, so `"user:{usrId}"` becomes `"user:{userId}"`.

## MCG010

`[assembly: CacheInterface]` names a type MethodCache can't decorate: a class, a generic interface, an interface that
is not accessible, one with static abstract members, or one declared in your own project (put `[Cache]` on its methods
instead). It is also reported when the attribute lists no methods. See the [third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MCG011

`[assembly: CacheInterface]` lists a method that is missing, overloaded, or returns nothing to cache. Use
`nameof(IClient.Method)` so a rename is caught by the compiler. See the
[third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MCG012

The same interface is listed in more than one `[assembly: CacheInterface]`. List each interface once, with all its
methods in the same attribute.

## MCG013

The interface has static abstract members, so no class can implement it as a decorator. Move the cached methods to an
interface without them.

## MCG014

`[Cache]` on a method returning `IEnumerable<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`. The cached value would be
the lazy sequence itself, which runs the query again on every enumeration. Return a materialized collection, such as
`Task<List<T>>`, `Task<IReadOnlyList<T>>` or `T[]`, and call `ToListAsync()` (or similar) in the implementation.

## MCG015

A tag has braces that look like a template but don't hold a plain parameter name: a property path such as
`"product:{product.Id}"`, spaces such as `"{ id }"`, or a format such as `"{day:yyyy-MM-dd}"`. Templates take a
parameter name only, so the braces stay literal text and every call shares the same tag. Write `"product:{id}"` and
add the value as its own parameter, as `UpdateAsync(int id, Product product)` does in
[Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md). For `[assembly: CacheInterface]` both MCG009 and MCG015 are reported on the
attribute.


---

<!-- source: docs/migration-from-imemorycache.md -->

# Migrating from IMemoryCache

With `IMemoryCache`, every cached method holds the same pattern: build a key, try the cache, load, store, and remember
every key to remove when data changes. MethodCache moves that into an attribute on the interface.

<table>
<tr><th>Before: IMemoryCache</th><th>After: MethodCache</th></tr>
<tr><td>

```cs
public async Task<User> GetUserAsync(int id)
{
    var key = $"user:{id}";
    if (_cache.TryGetValue(key, out User? user))
        return user!;

    // Two callers can both miss and both hit the database
    user = await _db.LoadUserAsync(id);
    _cache.Set(key, user, TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10));
    return user;
}

public async Task RenameAsync(int id, string name)
{
    await _db.RenameAsync(id, name);
    _cache.Remove($"user:{id}");
    // ...and every other key that held this user
}
```

</td><td>

```cs
[Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["user:{id}"])]
Task<User> GetUserAsync(int id);

[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["user:{id}"])]
Task RenameAsync(int id, string name);
```

</td></tr>
</table>

## Steps

1. Add the `MethodCache` package and call `builder.Services.AddMethodCache()` after your registrations
   ([Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)).
2. If the class has no interface, extract one. Callers must use the interface, because the cache is a decorator around
   it.
3. Move the caching settings to `[Cache]` on the interface method, and delete the cache code from the implementation.
4. Replace each `Remove(key)` with `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` on the method that changes the data, and give the
   cached methods matching tags ([Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md)).
5. Code that can't move to an attribute, such as a cached call in the middle of a method, uses
   `ICacheManager.GetOrCreateAsync` with the key it already has ([Manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md)).

Migrate one service at a time; both caches can run side by side.

## What maps to what

| IMemoryCache | MethodCache |
|--------------|-------------|
| `TryGetValue` + `Set` | `[Cache]`, or `GetOrCreateAsync` with your key |
| `SetAbsoluteExpiration` | `Duration` |
| `SetSlidingExpiration` | `SlidingExpiration`, capped by `Duration` |
| `Remove(key)` | `[CacheInvalidate]` with tags, or `InvalidateByKeysAsync` |
| `Size` and `SizeLimit` | `Weigher` and `MaxMemoryBytes` ([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md)) |
| `Priority` | Not needed: W-TinyLFU keeps the entries that are read often |
| `GetOrCreateAsync`, which may run the factory several times at once | Concurrent misses share one call |
| A separate `IDistributedCache` | `AddMethodCacheRedis(...)`, with the memory cache kept in sync ([Distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md)) |

## Differences to know

- **Keys are generated** from the method and its arguments ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md)). Check that every argument
  that changes the result is a parameter, not a field of the class.
- **`null` is cached** by default. Set `CacheNullValues = false` if your old code skipped `null`.
- **Exceptions are never cached**, as before.


---

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.Redis/README.md -->

# MethodCache.Redis

Redis as MethodCache's distributed cache. Results are shared between application instances, and invalidations reach every instance's in-memory cache over Redis pub/sub.

## Usage

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis("localhost:6379");
```

With options:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis(options =>
{
    options.Configuration = "redis1:6379,redis2:6379,password=...";
    options.KeyPrefix = "orders-api:";   // the backplane channel follows: orders-api:invalidations
});
```

MethodCache keeps its own cache and connection, so your app's `IDistributedCache` and Redis settings are left alone. The connection opens on first use, so the application starts while Redis is down. It uses `BacklogPolicy.FailFast`, so a cache miss runs your method instead of waiting for Redis.

To share a connection your app already has instead:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis(options =>
    options.ConnectionMultiplexerFactory = sp => sp.GetRequiredService<IConnectionMultiplexer>());
```

MethodCache doesn't dispose a shared connection.

## How it works

- Entries are stored through `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis`, so values are written without extra copies.
- Values are JSON written with System.Text.Json; add `MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack` and call `AddMethodCacheMessagePack()` for MessagePack. Each entry records its format, so after a switch older entries count as misses.
- MethodCache reads Redis on an in-memory miss and writes new results to both.
- Invalidating a key removes it from Redis. Invalidating a tag stores the time of the invalidation, and entries with that tag written before it are treated as missing, so no tag sets are kept in Redis.
- Both also publish a message, so every instance drops its in-memory copies at once.
- Pub/sub delivers nothing while a connection is down. When the connection comes back, the instance clears its in-memory cache and reads entries from Redis again.
- Pattern invalidation (`InvalidateByTagPatternAsync`) is not supported with a distributed cache and throws `NotSupportedException`.

## When Redis is down

MethodCache keeps answering from memory and your methods; Redis never fails or stalls a call.

- Every Redis call is capped at `OperationTimeout` (1 second).
- After a failure or timeout, MethodCache skips Redis for `CircuitBreakerDuration` (10 seconds), then one call checks whether it is back. The first failure and the recovery are logged.
- Invalidations that Redis doesn't accept are queued and retried until it does. They never throw. Until they are stored, this instance doesn't read entries from Redis, so an invalidated value can't come back.
- `ClockSkewTolerance` (2 seconds) covers servers whose clocks differ: a tag invalidation also applies to entries created up to that long after it.

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<DistributedCacheOptions>(options =>
{
    options.OperationTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500);
    options.CircuitBreakerDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);
});
```

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `Configuration` | `localhost:6379` | StackExchange.Redis configuration string |
| `ConnectionMultiplexerFactory` | none | Returns an existing connection to share instead of opening one |
| `KeyPrefix` | `methodcache:` | Prefix for every key MethodCache writes |
| `EnableBackplane` | `true` | Send invalidations to other instances over pub/sub |
| `BackplaneChannel` | `KeyPrefix` + `invalidations` | Pub/sub channel; applications with different key prefixes get different channels |


---

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.SqlServer/README.md -->

# MethodCache.SqlServer

SQL Server as MethodCache's distributed cache. Results are shared between application instances, and invalidations reach every instance's in-memory cache through a table that each instance polls.

## Usage

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheSqlServer(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Cache")!);
```

With options:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheSqlServer(options =>
{
    options.ConnectionString = connectionString;
    options.SchemaName = "cache";
    options.BackplanePollingInterval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500);
});
```

## Tables

By default the schema and two tables are created when the application starts, if they do not exist. Startup waits at most three seconds for that; if SQL Server is down, creation is retried in the background and methods run uncached until it succeeds.

- `MethodCache` holds the entries, in the layout `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.SqlServer` uses (the same as `dotnet sql-cache create`).
- `MethodCacheInvalidations` holds recent invalidations for the backplane.

If the application's login may not create tables, set `CreateTablesIfMissing = false` and create them in a migration instead.

## How it works
