- Entries are stored through MethodCache's own `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.SqlServer` cache, which also removes expired rows. Your app's `IDistributedCache` is left alone.
- Values are JSON written with System.Text.Json; add `MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack` and call `AddMethodCacheMessagePack()` for MessagePack.
- MethodCache reads SQL Server on an in-memory miss and writes new results to both.
- Invalidating a key removes its row. Invalidating a tag stores the time of the invalidation, and entries with that tag written before it are treated as missing, so no tag tables are needed.
- Both also add a row to the invalidations table. Other instances read new rows every `BackplanePollingInterval` and drop their in-memory copies.
- Rows older than `BackplaneRetention` are deleted from the invalidations table.
- An instance that couldn't read the invalidations table for half of `BackplaneRetention` may have missed invalidations, so it clears its in-memory cache.
- Pattern invalidation (`InvalidateByTagPatternAsync`) is not supported with a distributed cache and throws `NotSupportedException`.

## When SQL Server is down

MethodCache keeps answering from memory and your methods; SQL Server never fails or stalls a call.

- Every SQL Server call is capped at `OperationTimeout` (1 second).
- After a failure or timeout, MethodCache skips SQL Server for `CircuitBreakerDuration` (10 seconds), then one call checks whether it is back. The first failure and the recovery are logged.
- Invalidations that SQL Server doesn't accept are queued and retried until it does. They never throw. Until they are stored, this instance doesn't read entries from SQL Server, so an invalidated value can't come back.
- `ClockSkewTolerance` (2 seconds) covers servers whose clocks differ: a tag invalidation also applies to entries created up to that long after it.

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<DistributedCacheOptions>(options =>
{
    options.OperationTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500);
    options.CircuitBreakerDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);
});
```

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `ConnectionString` | (required) | SQL Server connection string |
| `SchemaName` | `dbo` | Schema of both tables |
| `TableName` | `MethodCache` | Table for cache entries |
| `InvalidationsTableName` | `MethodCacheInvalidations` | Table the backplane uses |
| `KeyPrefix` | `methodcache:` | Prefix for every key MethodCache writes |
| `CreateTablesIfMissing` | `true` | Create the schema and tables at startup |
| `EnableBackplane` | `true` | Share invalidations with other instances |
| `BackplanePollingInterval` | 1 second | How often each instance reads new invalidations |
| `BackplaneRetention` | 1 hour | How long invalidations are kept; at least one minute |


---

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.AspNetCore/README.md -->

# MethodCache.AspNetCore

Admin endpoints and a health check for MethodCache's in-memory cache.

## Setup

```cs
builder.Services.AddScoped<IUserService, UserService>();
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddAuthorization(o => o.AddPolicy("CacheAdmins", p => p.RequireRole("Admin")));

var app = builder.Build();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapMethodCacheAdmin("CacheAdmins");
app.MapHealthChecks("/health");
```

The authorization policy is required, because the endpoints expose cache keys and can empty the cache; a
signed-in user without the policy gets 403.

## Endpoints

All paths are relative to the prefix (`/methodcache` by default).

| Method | Path | What it does |
|--------|------|--------------|
| `GET` | `stats` | Hits, misses, hit ratio, evictions, entries and estimated memory |
| `GET` | `methods` | The effective policy of every cached method and where it came from |
| `GET` | `entries?prefix=&tag=&limit=` | Live entries ordered by key (default limit 100, max 1000). Values are not returned |
| `GET` | `entry?key=` | One entry, or 404 |
| `DELETE` | `entry?key=` | Removes one entry, or 404 |
| `POST` | `invalidate` | Removes entries by tag. Body: `{ "tags": ["users"] }` |
| `DELETE` | `entries` | Removes every entry |

The same operations are available in code through `ICacheAdministrator` in the `MethodCache` namespace.

## Health check

`AddMethodCache()` on the health checks builder reports Healthy when the cache answers, with `entries`,
`hitRatio`, `evictions` and `memoryUsageBytes` in the report data. With Redis or SQL Server it reports Degraded
while that cache is unreachable and MethodCache serves from memory only (`distributedCacheAvailable` in the data).
Each check asks the distributed cache once, waiting at most its operation timeout.

## Limits

- Works with the default in-memory cache manager. A custom `ICacheManager` has no `ICacheAdministrator`.
- Policies are read-only here. Change them at runtime with `IRuntimeCacheConfigurator`.


---

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.OpenTelemetry/README.md -->

# MethodCache.OpenTelemetry

[![NuGet Version](https://img.shields.io/nuget/v/MethodCache.OpenTelemetry)](https://www.nuget.org/packages/MethodCache.OpenTelemetry)

OpenTelemetry metrics and traces for MethodCache.

The package depends only on the OpenTelemetry API, as instrumentation libraries should, so it works the same in
console apps, workers and ASP.NET Core. Your app brings the SDK and exporters. For request spans, add
`OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore` to your app as usual.

## What you get

- **Metrics for every call**:
  - hits, misses and errors per method;
  - how long the cached method took on a miss;
  - entries, memory and hit ratio of the in-memory cache.
- **Spans for misses and invalidations**:
  - Each span has the method, hit or miss, TTL, group, version and the cache tags.
  - Spans are children of the current request span and copy its `http.*` and `url.*` attributes.
- **Hits stay allocation-free**: generated decorators answer hits from the cache's fast path, which has no span. Hits still count in `methodcache.hits_total`.

## Installation

```bash
dotnet add package MethodCache.OpenTelemetry
dotnet add package OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting   # the SDK and AddOpenTelemetry(), if your app doesn't have it yet
```

## Setup

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheOpenTelemetry(); // after AddMethodCache, which registers the cache it instruments

builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
    .WithTracing(tracing => tracing
        .AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()
        .AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()
        .AddOtlpExporter())
    .WithMetrics(metrics => metrics
        .AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()
        .AddOtlpExporter());
```

Sampling, export intervals and the service name are set on the OpenTelemetry SDK as for any other library.

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
|--------|---------|--------------|
| `EnableTracing` | `true` | Creates spans |
| `EnableMetrics` | `true` | Records metrics |
| `RecordCacheKeys` | `false` | Puts the cache key on spans. Keys can contain argument values |
| `HashCacheKeys` | `true` | With `RecordCacheKeys`, records a hash of the key instead of the key |
| `ExportSensitiveData` | `false` | Puts the user and tenant ids from `IBaggagePropagator` into span baggage |
| `EnableHttpCorrelation` | `true` | Copies the request's `http.*` and `url.*` attributes onto cache spans |
| `EnableBaggagePropagation` | `true` | Carries `cache.*` baggage between spans |

## Baggage

`IBaggagePropagator` carries a correlation id, an invalidation id, a user id and a tenant id along the async flow,
and puts them into the baggage of cache spans, which travels to downstream services. The user and tenant ids
identify people, so they are left out unless `ExportSensitiveData` is on. A value set in a child task stays in that
task.

```cs
_baggagePropagator.SetCacheCorrelationId(Guid.NewGuid().ToString());
_baggagePropagator.SetCacheTenantId(tenantId); // exported only with ExportSensitiveData = true
```

## Span attributes

| Attribute | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `cache.method` | Method name | `IUserService.GetUserAsync` |
| `cache.hit` | Whether the value came from the cache | `true` |
| `cache.key` / `cache.key_hash` | The key, with `RecordCacheKeys` | `a1b2c3d4` |
| `cache.ttl_seconds` | Time-to-live | `600` |
| `cache.tags` | Cache tags | `user,profile` |
| `cache.group` | Group | `users` |
| `cache.version` | Version | `2` |
| `cache.keys_count` | Number of keys invalidated | `3` |

## Metrics

Metric dimensions are kept to values with few variants (`method`, `group`, `version`, `error.type`), so a tag such
as `user:42` never becomes a time series of its own.

| Metric | Type | Description | Dimensions |
|--------|------|-------------|------------|
| `methodcache.hits_total` | Counter | Cache hits, including fast-path hits | method |
| `methodcache.misses_total` | Counter | Cache misses | method |
| `methodcache.errors_total` | Counter | Errors (`load_failed` when the cached method throws) | method, error.type |
| `methodcache.load_duration` | Histogram (ms) | Time the cached method took on a miss or refresh | method |
| `methodcache.operation_duration` | Histogram (ms) | Duration of instrumented operations (misses, invalidations) | method, group, version |
| `methodcache.key_generation_duration` | Histogram (ms) | Key generation on instrumented operations | method |
| `methodcache.entries_count` | Gauge | Entries in the in-memory cache | |
| `methodcache.memory_bytes` | Gauge | Estimated memory of the in-memory cache | |
| `methodcache.hit_ratio` | Gauge | Hits / (hits + misses) | |

## Troubleshooting

**No spans.** Check that the SDK listens to the source with `.AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()` on the tracer
provider. `TracingConstants.ActivitySource.HasListeners()` is true once it does.

**No HTTP attributes on cache spans.** Cache spans copy them from the request span, so enable ASP.NET Core
instrumentation: `.WithTracing(t => t.AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation().AddMethodCacheInstrumentation())`.
